title: Why a generator makes alternating current
examples: Why does a generator make AC?
What does 50 hertz mean for mains electricity?

marks.label: Reversed voltage
marks.ask: Why does a generator make alternating current?

explain.say: Spin a magnet near a coil of wire and electricity appears, with no battery at all! That is called electromagnetic induction. Every power station uses it. But the current it makes keeps flipping direction. Let us watch why.

draw.text: Why a generator makes alternating current

marks.label: Reversed voltage
marks.ask: Why does a generator make alternating current?

explain.say: Picture a coil spinning between two magnets. As its sides cut through the magnetic field, a voltage is pushed out. Look at the first dot: the coil sides are cutting the field fastest, so the voltage is at its peak. When is the voltage biggest?

marks.label: Reversed voltage
marks.ask: Why does a generator make alternating current?

explain.say: When the sides cut the field fastest, yes! A quarter turn later, the coil lies flat and its sides slide along the field, not across it. See the dot on the middle line? The voltage is zero for an instant. Where is the voltage zero?

marks.label: Reversed voltage
marks.ask: Why does a generator make alternating current?

explain.say: Right on the middle line! Now the coil has flipped over, so each side moves through the field the other way. Look at the next dot: the voltage is reversed. Back and forth, every turn. That is alternating current, or AC. Which way does it flow now?

marks.label: Reversed voltage
marks.ask: Why does a generator make alternating current?

explain.say: The opposite way, perfect! One full turn makes one full wave. Mains in India, Nigeria and the UK makes 50 waves every second, 50 hertz; the USA and Brazil use 60. Wow fact: Japan uses both, 50 hertz in the east and 60 in the west! Challenge: what does spinning faster do?

marks.label: Reversed voltage
marks.ask: Why does a generator make alternating current?

faq.a: The voltage is biggest when the coil sides cut across the magnetic field lines fastest, moving at right angles to them.
asks: When is the induced voltage largest?

faq.q: Why does a generator make alternating current?
faq.a: Each half turn, the coil sides swap places and move through the field in the opposite direction, so the induced current reverses.
The current changes direction and back 50 times every second, so 50 full waves per second.
When a wire moves through a magnetic field, or the field around it changes, a voltage is induced in the wire.

faq.q: How can a generator make more voltage?
faq.a: Spin it faster, use stronger magnets or add more turns to the coil. Spinning faster also raises the frequency.
asks: How do you increase the output of a generator?

facts: Mains electricity is 50 Hz in India, the UK and Nigeria, and 60 Hz in the USA and Brazil.
Japan uses 50 Hz in the east and 60 Hz in the west.

quiz.say: In a spinning coil generator, when is the voltage zero?
quiz.show: In a spinning coil generator, when is the voltage zero?

options.show: When the coil sides move along the field
options.say: When the coil sides move along the field

options.show: When the sides cut the field fastest
options.say: When the sides cut the field fastest

quiz.why: Moving along the field lines cuts none of them, so no voltage is induced at that moment.

wrong.1: That is when the voltage is biggest.
wrong.2: It is zero for an instant twice every turn.
